paragraphs.text: God’s free grace and favour is fitly premised, as the fountain and mother of all the following mercies. This is that other book, Rev 20:12, that hath our names in it, and our pardon.
paragraphs.anchor: Lord, thou hast been favourable, &c.

paragraphs.text: Of old from Egypt, and alate from the Philistines; who, after Saul’s death, miserably tyrannized over Israel, till David delivered them. Some hold that this psalm was composed at the end of the Babylonish captivity; others conceive it may be a prayer for the conversion of the Gentiles, who are brought in speaking, the whole psalm throughout.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob

paragraphs.text: This is worthily mentioned as a main mercy, as a chief fruit of free grace.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou hast forgiven the iniquity, &c.

paragraphs.text: That that filthy thing may be no longer an eyesore unto thee. In the original there are six homoioteleuta, which is an elegancy not to be translated into English.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou hast covered all their sins

paragraphs.text: Heb. thou hast gathered it, thou hast recollected it, that we might not bear it; when sin is once remitted, wrath is soon removed.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou hast taken away all thy wrath

paragraphs.text: Here are six hasts drawing in the next turn, Psa 85:4. God hath, and therefore God will, is a strong medium of hope, if not a demonstration of Scripture logics. See 2Co 1:10.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou hast turned thyself from the fierceness, &c.

paragraphs.text: Turn us, and we shall be turned; do as thou ever hast done, for thou art Jehovah, thou changest not, but art yesterday, today, and the same for ever.
paragraphs.anchor: Turn us, O God of our salvation

paragraphs.text: Labefacta iram tuam erga nos.
paragraphs.anchor: And cause thine anger, &c.

paragraphs.text: Dilato Christo tuo vel tuo adventu? Such expostulations mixed with faith are Vis Deo grata, as saith Tertullian, such as God is well pleased with.
paragraphs.anchor: Wilt thou be angry with us for ever?

paragraphs.text: Who for present are all amort, as it were, free among the dead? free of that company?
paragraphs.anchor: Wilt thou not revive us again?

paragraphs.text: A joyless life is a lifeless life, Mortis habet vices quae trahitur vita gemitibus.
paragraphs.anchor: That thy people may rejoice in thee

paragraphs.text: Thy fatherly mercy, στοργην.
paragraphs.anchor: Show us thy mercy, O Lord

paragraphs.text: Thy Christ, and our Jesus, Luk 2:30.
paragraphs.anchor: And grant us thy salvation

paragraphs.text: I will not repine, but listen what answer God giveth to my prayer, and patiently wait a good issue of my troubles.
paragraphs.anchor: I will hear what God the Lord will speak

paragraphs.text: viz. By his promises, and by his providences.
paragraphs.anchor: For he will speak peace unto his people

paragraphs.text: For all God’s people are righteous ones, Isa 60:21, justified and sanctified, 1Co 6:11.
paragraphs.anchor: And, to his saints

paragraphs.text: i.e. To the ways of the world and of carnal reason, lest they smart for their rashness, and God never take their words again.
paragraphs.anchor: But let them not turn again to folly

paragraphs.text: Though they be so bleared oft with tears that they cannot see it, and so discouraged that they have even done looking for it, Luk 18:7-8.
paragraphs.anchor: Surely his salvation is nigh them, &c.

paragraphs.text: The Fathers both by salvation and glory dwelling with men understand Christ, Joh 1:16.
paragraphs.anchor: That glory may dwell in our land

paragraphs.text: As in God (his mercy is ever bounded by his truth), so in all his people, there is a sweet conjunction and concatenation of graces, 2Pe 1:5; and this is an effect of Christ’s kingdom in men’s hearts, Rom 14:17, Iam fides et pax, et honor pudorque Priscus, et neglecta redire virtus Audet; apparetque beata pleno Copia cornu (Horat.).
paragraphs.anchor: Mercy and truth are met together

paragraphs.text: Have friendly saluted, in allusion to the manner of the Eastern nations. See Isa 32:17 Psa 119:105.
paragraphs.anchor: Righteousness and peace have kissed each other

paragraphs.text: i.e. Heaven and earth shall be full both of truth and righteousness. Many understand all concerning Christ. See Joh 3:13. Others, concerning extraordinary plenty of all good things.
paragraphs.anchor: Truth shall spring out of the earth

paragraphs.text: Yea, best of all, viz. his Holy Spirit (Luk 11:13, with Mat 7:11), with a largess of outward comforts.
paragraphs.anchor: Yea, the Lord shall give that which is good

paragraphs.text: Men shall walk before God in holiness and righteousness all the days of their lives, Luk 1:75; they shall not rest in outward blessings, Psa 85:12, or be satisfied with such low things, but be led up thereby to the care of higher.
paragraphs.anchor: Righteousness shall go before him

paragraphs.text: So that we shall go an upper (and therefore a better) way, Pro 15:24, having our feet where other men’s heads are; and so departing from hell beneath, which even gapeth for the unrighteous.
paragraphs.anchor: And shall set us in the way of his steps
